correctness.rationale: For the finite primorial wheel N=product_{p<=P}p (P prime >=5), CRT factorizes each additive character into local residues. At p=2 its factor has modulus one, at odd p the factors are p-2 for local frequency 0 and -1-e^{4pi ib/p} otherwise; none vanishes since p is odd. The independent local log magnitudes have exact mean log(p-2)/p and variance as displayed. Product identity at -1 makes the sum of nonzero logarithms zero, while the L2 Fourier series of log(2|cos pi u|) gives asymptotic per-prime variance pi²/12 and bounded third absolute moments. Aperiodic CRT and Berry-Esseen then give the uniform O(pi(P)^(-1/2)) CLT, and conjugate eigenvalue pairing with two real eigenvalues of opposite sign yields the negative circulant determinant. Independent direct DFT calculations at N=30,210 and an exact 30x30 integer determinant -729 match.
residual_risks: This is Fourier behavior of a finite candidate mask, not the Fourier transform or infinitude of genuine twin primes.
The Riemann-sum error near a cosine-log singularity is a nontrivial estimate, though its stated bounded-variation bound is consistent; no optimized Berry-Esseen constant.

originality.rationale: Holt studies exact sieving cycles and admissible constellation population recurrences, which are the same combinatorial setting but different observables. Standard CRT supplies each Fourier factor and Berry-Esseen supplies a generic Gaussian method, but neither establishes this joint exact spectral product, mean/variance constants, all-frequency quantitative CLT and signed determinant. Resultary search found no stronger matching mask-Fourier theorem. Priority is qualified because the full Holt article could not be inspected through arXiv/OA or institutional VPN.
